name: Technical indicator bots (freqtrade, Zenbot sample strategies)

origin.authors: Zenbot (2016) and freqtrade (2017) communities; academic test by Hudson and Urquhart
origin.source_title: Technical trading and cryptocurrencies (Annals of Operations Research 2021)

how_it_works.simple: A program watches price charts and buys or sells when lines like moving averages or RSI cross certain levels.
how_it_works.analogy: Like a thermostat that turns the heat on and off at set temperatures, whether or not the weather pattern has changed.
how_it_works.precise: Rules built from moving averages, RSI, Bollinger bands, MACD and similar indicators on 1-minute to 1-day candles, often tuned with hyperparameter search (freqtrade hyperopt). Hudson and Urquhart test about 15,000 rules with multiple-testing corrections.

rule: Example freqtrade-style rule: on 5-minute candles, buy when RSI(14) < 30 and the fast EMA crosses above the slow EMA; sell when RSI > 70 or a fixed stop loss or take profit is hit.
economic_rationale: Detzel et al. (2021) argue technical rules can be rational when fundamentals are hard to value, as with bitcoin.
why_it_might_fail: Zenbot's README says default parameters will underperform buy-and-hold; freqtrade's docs say lookahead bias is easy to introduce and makes biased strategies look very profitable. Hudson and Urquhart find no predictability for Bitcoin out of sample.

reported_results.source: Hudson and Urquhart (2021), abstract (open access copy)
reported_results.period: CoinDesk BTC from 2010-07-18; other coins from later start dates
reported_results.market: Two BTC markets plus three other coins
reported_results.notes: In-sample: significant predictability for all five rule classes after data-snooping corrections, with breakeven costs above typical crypto costs. Out-of-sample: 'no predictability for Bitcoin', though some remains in other coins.
README states default trade parameters will underperform a buy-hold strategy and that the project is no longer maintained (repo archived).

post_publication_evidence: Hudson and Urquhart's out-of-sample period shows no Bitcoin predictability. Zenbot was archived in 2022. Freqtrade added lookahead and recursive analysis tools because user strategies often contain leakage.

implementations.notes: Active; includes backtesting, hyperopt, FreqAI, lookahead-analysis.
Community sample strategies, explicitly not vetted for profit.

relevance.reason: Freqtrade is good test plumbing, but indicator rules themselves show little out-of-sample edge on the main liquid asset.
